task_scope: Focused source acquisition only for Tennessee 2026 general-election U.S. Senate write-in certificates. No source admission, candidate/model/input changes, guessed IDs, outreach, or inference from absent names.

prior_evidence_reviewed.relevant_prior_conclusion: TN unclear: Nashville official rule but no named roster; accessible ordinary candidate lists do not establish qualified-write-in coverage.

prior_evidence_reviewed.relevant: Owner forecast cutoff 2026-10-20; Oct 25 retrieval cannot establish cutoff-time availability.
Nashville official rule states timely certificate requirement and bars same-office primary losers; no named roster.

outcome.finding: Acquired an official Sumner County Election Commission-hosted Tennessee Certificate of Write-In Candidacy (state form SS-3072). The form provides materially relevant filing/geographic scope: for general-election Governor, U.S. Senate, and U.S. House, a certificate must be filed in each county comprising the office's district; the special central-Coordinator route stated on this form is for those offices in primary elections. It is a blank form, not a 2026 candidate certificate or roster, so it names no candidate and cannot establish any candidate's eligibility or nonexistence.
outcome.statewide_scope_requirement: For 2026 general-election U.S. Senate, the form's county-per-district rule applies across Tennessee's 95 counties. To establish a statewide named qualified write-in menu, obtain an official consolidated certificate roster explicitly covering all 95 counties or county filing/receipt records with completeness scope. A certificate filed in fewer than all counties can still support counting only in counties where timely filed, so statewide totals cannot be presumed from one county.
outcome.deadline: The form states noon prevailing time on the 50th day before the election. For Nov. 3, 2026, that date was Sep. 14, 2026. Deadline passage does not establish zero filings.
outcome.no_absence_inference: No named candidate is inferred from the blank form, generic ballot write-in slots, or absence from ordinary printed candidate lists.
